newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates up but advances rate seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates up but advances rate seen steady.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose further on Friday, but dealers said the gap of over 30 basis points between the call rate and the central bank's special advances rate did not demand a rise in the advances rate.
Call money was bid at 2.81-2.87 percent versus 2.62 percent a day earlier.
The Dutch central bank will set a new special advances pact at 1400 GMT, which is currently set at 2.50 percent.
"The special advances rate will remain unchanged for the remaining months of this year," said one dealer. Another dealer said he too did not expect a change in the near-term.
All deposit rates were a fraction higher. Dealers said this was partly offset by a weaker guilder against the mark, with others noting guilder-deposits rose in dollar-swap trade.
The guilder was trading at 112.21 per 100 marks from 112.195 on Thursday.
Three-month deposits rose four basis points to 2.76 percent bid and one-year deposits added two basis points to 3.00 percent bid.
Volumes were low with business focusing on the shorter end of the curve.
